subtopics.title: Buying on Credit — the Invoice Received and the CJ

questions.question: Thabo buys stock on credit from Metro. In THABO'S books, Metro is:
options: A creditor — a liability, money the business owes

questions.question: The source document for the Creditors Journal is:
options: The invoice received from the supplier, renumbered into the business's own sequence
A credit note issued by the business

questions.question: The CJ deliberately has NO cost of sales column because:
options: The column exists but is rarely used
Buying loads the shelf at cost — one truth; the two-truths pair belongs to selling
Cost of sales is recorded weekly instead

subtopics.title: Recording and Posting the Creditors Journal

questions.question: The R3 000 display shelving from ShelfCo is analysed to:
options: Equipment — an asset kept for use

questions.question: Metro's personal account is CREDITED R9 000 on the 3rd because:
options: Creditors are liabilities, and liabilities grow on the credit side — the business owes more

questions.question: The CJ's month-end posting to the general ledger is:
options: Debit Creditors Control 12 400; credit the analysis accounts
Credit Creditors Control 12 400; debit Trading Stock 9 000, Stationery 400, Equipment 3 000

questions.question: The CJ's cross-cast requires:
options: Trading Stock + Stationery + Equipment (+ Sundries) totals to equal the Creditors Control total
All personal accounts to equal each other
The invoice numbers to be sequential

subtopics.title: Returns to Suppliers — the Debit Note and the CAJ

questions.question: When returning damaged goods to a supplier, the business issues:
options: A debit note — its own numbered document reducing the supplier's account

questions.question: The CAJ's totals (Creditors Control R900; Trading Stock R800; Stationery R100) post as:
options: Credit Creditors Control; debit the analysis accounts
Debit Bank R900; credit Creditors Control R900
Debit Creditors Control R900; credit Trading Stock R800 and Stationery R100

questions.question: A return to a supplier involves NO movement of money because:
options: Returns adjust the debt; payment is a separate event in a separate journal
Money moved when the goods were bought

subtopics.title: The Creditors Ledger, the List, and the Discipline of Paying

questions.question: Metro: credit 9 000, debit 800. The balance is:
options: R8 200 credit — the business owes Metro R8 200

questions.question: The list of creditors (8 200 + 300 + 3 000 = 11 500) must equal:
options: The Creditors Control balance: credit 12 400 minus debit 900 = R11 500

questions.question: Why is paying suppliers NEEDLESSLY EARLY also poor discipline?
options: Supplier credit is free financing — cash surrendered early was cash the business was entitled to use all month
It is never poor discipline — earlier is always better

subtopics.title: The Other Side of the Counter

questions.question: When Thabo buys on credit from Metro, in METRO'S books Thabo is:
options: A debtor — a name on a page in their debtors ledger

questions.question: The flip between the two books is best stated as:
options: Debtors grow on credit; creditors on debit
Debtor balances mean money coming in someday (debit side); creditor balances mean money going out someday (credit side)
Both books grow on the same side
Creditors are recorded only at year end

questions.question: Which features survive the flip unchanged?
options: The side on which pages grow
Pages per name, one summary line, daily detail, monthly totals, and the list-equals-control lock

subtopics.title: The Month of Buying on Trust

questions.question: Stock R9 000, stationery R400, shelving R3 000 — their homes are:
The debit note is described as 'the letter with numbers' because:
options: It contains the supplier's phone number
It is Thabo's own numbered document stating exactly how much he is reducing what he owes, and why

questions.question: After the returns, the pages read Metro R8 200, PNA R300, ShelfCo R3 000. The lock clicks when:
options: The pages total R11 500 and Creditors Control also shows R11 500
The bank balance matches the pages
The debit notes equal the invoices

questions.question: Invoiced for ten boxes, but the signed delivery note shows nine. The correct move is:
options: Pay the invoice and hope for the best
Pay for nine and say nothing
A debit-note query — mismatches are conversations, not payments

questions.question: 'On terms, on time, exactly' protects the business because:
options: Late payment burns the relationship and credit record; early payment surrenders free financing

questions.question: The supplier's monthly statement should be:
options: Checked against the supplier's page in the business's own books — two independent records that must agree
